**Arsenal (home) vs Nottingham Forest in the Premier League, scheduled for November 23, 2024, at Emirates Stadium in London.**[[1]](https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Nov-23/nottingham-forest)[[1]](https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Nov-23/nottingham-forest)

This summary draws exclusively from information available before November 23, 2024, focusing on contextual factors beyond baseline team strength. ### Head-to-Head History
Arsenal hold a dominant historical record against Nottingham Forest across all competitions (over 100 matches total, with Arsenal winning 56, drawing 24, and losing 29). In the Premier League era specifically, Arsenal have won the large majority of encounters.[[2]](https://www.worldfootball.net/match-report/co91/england-premier-league/ma569669/nottingham-forest_arsenal-fc/head-to-head/)

Recent Premier League meetings (pre-2024/25 season) include:
- Arsenal 5-0 Nottingham Forest (October 30, 2022, at Emirates).[[3]](https://www.11v11.com/teams/arsenal/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Nottingham%20Forest/)
- Nottingham Forest have secured only two Premier League wins against Arsenal, both at home (City Ground): one in 1996 and one in 2023.[[4]](https://www.facebook.com/ArsenalFanaticsNews/posts/-arsenal-results-vs-nottingham-forest-at-the-city-ground-since-2000%EF%B8%8F-0-0-2025-1-/1429969099139896/)

Arsenal have been particularly strong at home against Forest in recent years. ### Recent Form/Results (Leading into the Match)
As of mid-November 2024:
- **Arsenal** had endured a poor recent Premier League run, including a 2-2 draw vs Liverpool (October 27), a 0-1 loss vs Newcastle United (November 2), and a 1-1 draw vs Chelsea (November 10). They sat fourth in the table, nine points behind leaders Liverpool after 11 games, and were seeking to end a four-game winless streak in the league.[[5]](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/arsenal/injury-news/injuries-and-suspensions/will-saka-rice-trossard-return-arsenal-injury-list-for-forest-clash_558545.html)
- **Nottingham Forest** were in strong form under their manager, with recent wins including 1-3 at Leicester City (October 25), 1-0 vs Crystal Palace (October 21), and 3-0 vs West Ham United (November 2), though they lost 1-3 at Newcastle (November 10). They were level on points with Arsenal after 11 matches.[[6]](https://www.espn.com/soccer/team/results/_/id/393/league/ENG.1/season/2024)

### Injuries and Suspensions
**Arsenal** (key doubts/outs as of November 20-22, 2024 previews):
- Ben White: Out (knee surgery; expected return mid-January 2025).[[5]](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/arsenal/injury-news/injuries-and-suspensions/will-saka-rice-trossard-return-arsenal-injury-list-for-forest-clash_558545.html)
- Bukayo Saka: Minor doubt (knock from Chelsea match); possible return for this game.[[5]](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/arsenal/injury-news/injuries-and-suspensions/will-saka-rice-trossard-return-arsenal-injury-list-for-forest-clash_558545.html)
- Declan Rice: Major doubt (foot issue); played through pain vs Chelsea but remained questionable.[[5]](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/arsenal/injury-news/injuries-and-suspensions/will-saka-rice-trossard-return-arsenal-injury-list-for-forest-clash_558545.html)
- Riccardo Calafiori: Major doubt (knee).[[5]](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/arsenal/injury-news/injuries-and-suspensions/will-saka-rice-trossard-return-arsenal-injury-list-for-forest-clash_558545.html)
- Takehiro Tomiyasu: Major doubt (knee).[[5]](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/arsenal/injury-news/injuries-and-suspensions/will-saka-rice-trossard-return-arsenal-injury-list-for-forest-clash_558545.html)
- Kieran Tierney: Major doubt (hamstring; returning to training).[[5]](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/arsenal/injury-news/injuries-and-suspensions/will-saka-rice-trossard-return-arsenal-injury-list-for-forest-clash_558545.html)
- Leandro Trossard: Minor doubt (knock).[[5]](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/arsenal/injury-news/injuries-and-suspensions/will-saka-rice-trossard-return-arsenal-injury-list-for-forest-clash_558545.html)
- No suspensions noted.[[5]](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/arsenal/injury-news/injuries-and-suspensions/will-saka-rice-trossard-return-arsenal-injury-list-for-forest-clash_558545.html)

**Nottingham Forest**:
- Chris Wood: Out (knee injury; had not featured since October).[[7]](https://www.reddit.com/r/Gunners/comments/1qefsba/prematch_thread_nottingham_forest_vs_arsenal_17th/)
- Other potential absences or limited availability noted in broader context (e.g., goalkeeper John Victor with knee issues in some reports), but specifics were less detailed in pre-match previews.[[8]](https://www.facebook.com/ArsenalFanaticsNews/posts/-injury-team-newsnottingham-forestoleksandr-zinchenko-d-out-ineligible-vs-parent/1428959769240829/)

### Travel, Fatigue, Venue, and Home Advantage
- **Travel/fatigue**: Forest’s trip from Nottingham to London is relatively short (~120 miles / ~2-2.5 hours by road or train), posing minimal fatigue risk compared to longer journeys. No major midweek European commitments were highlighted as issues immediately prior. - **Venue conditions**: Emirates Stadium (capacity ~60,000) in London—standard Premier League pitch and climate (mild autumn conditions expected; no notable altitude or weather extremes). Arsenal’s strong home record was a recurring theme in previews. - **Crowd/home advantage**: Significant factor favoring Arsenal, with the passionate Emirates atmosphere expected to support their push for a result amid their title-challenging ambitions.[[5]](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/arsenal/injury-news/injuries-and-suspensions/will-saka-rice-trossard-return-arsenal-injury-list-for-forest-clash_558545.html)

### Other Notable Storylines
- Arsenal were in a title race but had dropped points recently, making this a key opportunity to regain momentum before the festive period.[[5]](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/arsenal/injury-news/injuries-and-suspensions/will-saka-rice-trossard-return-arsenal-injury-list-for-forest-clash_558545.html)
- Forest had exceeded expectations with an excellent start, sitting level on points with Arsenal and aiming to build on their strong run. - No major external factors (e.g., weather disruptions, pitch issues, or off-field controversies) were prominently reported in pre-match coverage. Sources include contemporary previews and stats sites with data up to November 20-22, 2024 (e.g., Sports Mole injury updates, fixture listings, and historical records from 11v11/others). All details strictly predate the match date.

factors.impact: Arsenal holds a dominant historical record against Nottingham Forest, particularly at home, including a recent 5-0 victory at Emirates. This indicates a strong psychological and performance advantage against this specific opponent.
The match is at Emirates Stadium, where Arsenal benefits from a strong home record and passionate crowd support, which can be a significant boost for morale and performance.

Arsenal faces significant injury concerns, with key players like Declan Rice (major doubt) and Bukayo Saka (minor doubt) potentially missing or playing through pain. Ben White is out. These absences severely weaken their midfield and attack.
Arsenal is currently on a four-game winless streak in the Premier League, indicating a dip in momentum and confidence, which could impact their performance despite home advantage.

factors.factor: Nottingham Forest's Strong Recent Form & League Position
factors.impact: Nottingham Forest is in strong recent form and is notably level on points with Arsenal after 11 matches. This suggests they are a competitive opponent currently operating at a high level, diminishing Arsenal's assumed overall strength advantage.

analysis.reasoning: While Arsenal benefits from a historically dominant head-to-head record against Nottingham Forest, particularly at home, and a clear home advantage at the Emirates, these factors are significantly tempered by their current situation. Arsenal enters this match on a poor run of form, with a four-game winless streak in the league. More critically, they are grappling with a notable injury crisis, with pivotal players like Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka listed as major doubts. Conversely, Nottingham Forest arrives in strong form and, remarkably, sits level on points with Arsenal in the league table. This indicates Forest is performing well above typical expectations and will pose a stiff challenge. The net effect is a modest adjustment favoring Arsenal, acknowledging their historical superiority and home ground, but heavily moderated by their current struggles and Forest's strong, competitive standing this season.
